title: [Performance][MoE] Fuse shared W8A8 MXFP activation quantization with an explicit path
body:
### What this PR does / why we need it?

Shared experts using W8A8 MXFP run SwiGLU and activation MX quantization as separate kernels. Add an explicit `SharedExpertMLPPath.W8A8_MXFP_LINEAR` path that preserves both registered linears and fuses compatible activations with `npu_swiglu_group_quant(quant_mode=2)`.

The enum selects the implementation family, not a guarantee of fusion. After Gate-Up, `_prepare_w8a8_mxfp_down_input` checks the actual tensor and Down scheme. Compatible inputs produce `PreparedLinearInput`; the existing Down linear consumes its FP8 values and E8M0 scales without quantizing again. Unsupported inputs use the original activation and scheme-owned preparation. Active LoRA retains the generic wrapper path.

Fusion eligibility remains conservative: exact W8A8 MXFP scheme, plain SwiGLU, BF16 2D input, scale algorithm 0, 32-element groups, no TP input padding, parallel Down input, 128-element input-width alignment, and an available custom operator. Initialization consistency validation uses the same preparation helper.

Both linear-wrapper paths share the existing scheduling: activation/preparation follows `shared_activation_overlap_start`, and Down remains after the event recorded before routed combine (`routed_combine_start`). Gate-Up submission, expert gating, other quantization paths, and the main-branch fix for prequantized activation inputs are preserved.

For a `[36, 4096]` Gate-Up output, fusion removes one kernel launch and the write/read of a `[36, 2048]` BF16 intermediate (288 KiB of tensor traffic). End-to-end speedup requires NPU measurement.

### Does this PR introduce _any_ user-facing change?

No new public configuration or API. Compatible W8A8 MXFP shared experts use fused activation quantization; unsupported configurations retain their original preparation behavior.

### How was this patch tested?

- `python tests/ut/ops/test_shared_mxfp_activation.py -v`: all 14 dependency-free logic tests passed. They load the production enum and methods, with mocked tensor metadata/device calls, and cover dispatch, Gate-Up wrapper preservation, LoRA, generic and other fused paths, fusion/fallback event order, expert gating, aligned/unsupported inputs, initialization consistency, missing-operator fallback, and Down consumption without requantization.
- Updated existing CPU unit-test expectations for the explicit W8A8 MXFP path, including LoRA and incomplete weight initialization.
- Local Ruff, formatting, Codespell with repository settings, whitespace checks, and mypy for the contract tests targeting Python 3.10/3.11/3.12 passed.
- [GitHub CI on 4d5ee6559](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm-ascend/actions/runs/38433475205): full pre-commit (including repository hooks and mypy) passed; complete CPU unit-test jobs against vLLM main `8cc9aa5ad350f6f80cf3bebb298d410803ff75a9` and release `v0.30.0` both passed. DCO passed. The branch contains one linear commit so the CI rebase step also succeeds.
- NPU numerical parity, graph replay, and full-model performance require Ascend hardware. The repository requires a maintainer's test-enabling label before selected NPU tests can run.

- vLLM main: https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/commit/c4df37dfcc7f72ca41cd43801a468526ecf99a2b
